before.label: History Workshop movement
before.description: Develops collaborative history from below through adult education, labour movements, and historical scholarship. Its socialist and feminist projects involve worker-historians alongside academic historians. Oral testimony, women’s history, and later work on popular memory reshape its concerns.
before.representative_figures_and_works: Raphael Samuel; History Workshop Journal (1976 onward); Sheila Rowbotham, Hidden from History (1973); Samuel, Theatres of Memory (1994); Gareth Stedman Jones, Languages of Class (1983), a contested reorientation in British social history.

before.relationship: History Workshop provides publication and teaching settings for oral-history practice
before.evidence_note: Editorial synthesis supported by the listed bibliography; the specific relationship remains subject to passage-level review. Samuel’s 1976 article is checked at metadata level only. Becky Taylor’s firsthand recollection documents Anna Davin teaching oral history in 1998, supplying a concrete participant mechanism where the earlier link was generic. The full Samuel article remains unread.

after.relationship: History Workshop provides publication and teaching settings for oral-history practice
after.evidence_note: Editorial synthesis supported by the listed bibliography; the specific relationship remains subject to passage-level review. Samuel’s 1976 article is checked at metadata level only. Becky Taylor’s firsthand recollection documents Anna Davin teaching oral history in 1998, supplying a concrete participant mechanism where the earlier link was generic. The full Samuel article remains unread. Selected primary reprint passages now support Samuel’s specific methodological intervention, including his refusal to treat oral testimony as sufficient by itself. Original-printing collation remains unperformed.

verification.note: Read complete opening sections “Population and Power” and “Motherhood,” reprint 87–92; partial next section 93–94 encountered. Read reprint acknowledgment and chapter’s opening research-credit note. Original 1978 journal printing not collated; detailed later sections/notes unread. Credits identify Women against Population Control, History Workshop and Feminist History Group discussions, Walter Easey and the journal collective. Historical claims are Davin’s analysis, not independent validation of quoted public-health statistics or imperial racial categories.

outcomes.finding: Primary reprint passages replace title-only or retrospective support for the selected Samuel and Davin arguments. Original publication, later reprint and collaboration credits remain distinguished.
outcomes.research_limit: Samuel: reprint 208–210, opening 211, complete closing discussion 220–222 and notes 222–223 read. Intervening 211–219 incomplete. Burgess reader first appeared 1982; accessed transcription identifies 1989 impression/2005 electronic edition. Chapter credit identifies original 1976 article but notes include 1977 references; no exact original-printing equivalence asserted. Davin: complete opening sections, reprint 87–92, partial 93–94 and opening credit note read; later body/notes unread. 1997 acknowledgment identifies 1978 original; no original-printing collation. Credits do not substitute for worker-historians’ own writing under 048. No full-article or source-statistics verification claimed.
